name: In a Minute
tagline: Most people need a good reason to stop. You need one to hurry.
epigraph: Someone once put drinks like this in bottles for years, to see what time would do.
glassware: a small stemmed wine glass (about 200 ml), chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. The tagline lands as "a smile of being caught"; whoYouAre's frost in the fence's shadow and the lifelong "come on" carry the recognition. Barnum watch: "a small thing can make your day" is held by the scene and the guilt. Echoes moved off across the room: "a reason to stop" (jester-creator draft) → "a good reason to stop"; "Part of this glass…" (*Night Light*'s epigraph); "Then taste for it" (*Beside the First*'s closing shape); "a renowned classic" (*Not Only the Way*, *Next One's Mine*); the slow-living ending of her own plan sketch. The lint error "us" in yours 1 is fixed. Pronoun warnings accepted by Wren: every "he" and "his" is Conigliaro or Morgenthaler, never the guest. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/tony-conigliaro-aged-cocktails.md` (Robert Simonson, *A Proper Drink* pp. 228, 236; *Oxford Companion* BARREL-AGED COCKTAILS pdf 216–217, EL PRESIDENTE pdf 715–716, ALDEHYDES pdf 88, OXIDATION pdf 1458; Nate Tilden and Jeffrey Morgenthaler in Simonson's oral history, *PUNCH*, 19 June 2019, secondary; Portarias 38/2015 and 39/2015, *Jornal Oficial da Madeira*, read in the Portuguese original). Drink: David Wondrich, *Imbibe!* pdf 216–217; Gary Regan, *The Joy of Mixology* pdf 283; *Cocktail Codex* pp. 77, 251; Barbeito Rainwater 3 Anos producer's sheet (secondary) for the Madeira's figures. *Flavor Matrix*: no Madeira entry; consulted, set aside. Room notes: `work/explorer-innocent/`.
names_note: **In a Minute**, the room's pick (all three, r5): the guest's own answer to "come on", said kindly, and easy to order. Also considered: *Something in It* (Hester's runner-up, from y3's trust), *A Few Steps Behind*, *Take the Minute* (Tomás). Rejected: *Five Years* (the Manhattan's figure, not this drink's), *Aged*, *Bottle-Aged* (the method, and *Overnight*'s ground), *Worth Stopping For* (opening clash with *Worth the Trip*).
open_items: **No bottle-ageing in this glass, on purpose:** the plan's direction was a bottled drink the guest keeps; Tomás and Wren dropped it in round 2 (*For Good* closes on "make it a day ahead", *Overnight* owns time changing a drink). The time is in the glass as rainwater Madeira, a wine no one may sell until it has had about two years or more (Portaria 39/2015), on Conigliaro's own wine question (Oxford pdf 216).

**"Three years in oak" is not the law (Hester):** the *Codex*'s line for rainwater (p. 251) is a house belief; Portaria 38/2015 defines rainwater by colour and sweetness only. So the copy says "years", never oak. The closing line was changed in round 6 from "Nobody rushed that one" (estufagem heats the wine to hurry it) to "It took its time getting here", which claims only the wait.

**Morgenthaler (Hester C2, C4):** "impatient American" and "took the idea to the bank" are Simonson's words, not his, and are out; no source gives his own reason for switching to barrels. What spread was barrel-ageing in wood over weeks, not Conigliaro's years in glass, so the reading says "the idea spread". His own "it tasted like a Manhattan" (*PUNCH*) is the reading's turn, told without mockery. The barrel he used had held Madeira (Oxford pdf 217); the room kept that coincidence to the dossier.

**Dates (C1, C5):** 2004 is printed only in *Proper* p. 236, consistent with Oxford's five-year-old Manhattan tasted in 2009; the reading says "around 2004". Weeks, not "six weeks" (Oxford six, *Proper*'s Negroni seven).

**The recipe is ours:** 2:1 rum to vermouth (Oxford's and Regan's equal parts go OUT high on sugar and acid), white rum as Oxford prints it, Dolin Blanc recommended (Wondrich: "the last survivor" of the Chambéry style). The "answer to the Manhattan" is Wondrich's credit to Ribalaigua, whom Oxford calls only "quite possible". Madeira figures are Barbeito's (18.27%, 58 g/L, acidity 6.46 read as g/L tartaric); swept 0.5–0.9% acid, OUT only with the sharpest Madeira and grenadine together.
